summary: Changes the policy for the LoST Location Profiles IANA registry from Standards Action to Specification Required, so that standards bodies other than the IETF can add new values.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9036 changes the LoST Location Profiles registry from Standards Action to Specification Required. This lets other standards organizations propose values, subject to review of their need and documentation.

questions: who can add lost location profiles
what is specification required for the lost registry
what does the lost expert reviewer check
subtitle: Changes how new values are approved for the LoST Location Profiles registry.

tldr.problem: The LoST Location Profiles registry required Standards Action for every new value, while standards development organizations outside the IETF also needed to add values.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes the registration policy to Specification Required and assigns an Expert Reviewer to check the proposal's source, need, and clarity.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9036 updates RFC 5222 so standards development organizations other than the IETF can add profile values under review.

today: RFC 9036 is a Proposed Standard from June 2021 and updates RFC 5222.

sections.title: Why the Registration Policy Changed
sections.content:
The Location-to-Service Translation (LoST) protocol uses location profiles when conveying location, including in mapping requests and service boundary results. RFC 5222 established an IANA registry for these profiles with a Standards Action policy, which requires a Standards Track RFC for each new value.

The National Emergency Number Association (NENA), which uses LoST in emergency call specifications, identified a need for additional location profiles. RFC 9036 changes the policy to allow standards development organizations other than the IETF to add values.
sections.plainLanguage: LoST uses named location profiles, but its registry originally required an IETF standards action for every new entry. This update allows other standards organizations to propose entries.

sections.title: New Policy and Expert Review
sections.content:
The registry policy changes from Standards Action to Specification Required, as defined by RFC 8126. IANA lists RFC 9036 as a registry reference and uses an Expert Reviewer designated under RFC 8126.

The reviewer should check that the value is specified by the IETF, NENA, or a similar organization where location profiles are in scope; that there is a clear need and no existing profile meets it; and that the specification is unambiguous and interoperable.
sections.plainLanguage: A new value needs a written specification and an expert review. The reviewer checks that an appropriate organization defined it, that it fills a real need, and that its description is clear.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC identifies no new security considerations from changing the registry policy. The update concerns who may register new values in the LoST Location Profiles registry.
sections.plainLanguage: The change to the registration policy introduces no new security considerations, according to the RFC.
